manufacturer.observations: Manufacturer 2017 sheet distinguishes CTOL/CV versus STOVL ratings. Its dimensions are grouped into conventional engine and combined STOVL system columns; do not assign 9.37 m whole-system length to the isolated PW-600 main engine. Family inlet 43 in (1.09 m) supplies an approximate fan diameter only.
manufacturer.unresolved: No primary dimensioned PW-600 main-engine drawing, B-specific nozzle length or A8/A9 schedule was found. The source uses a nominal 5.44 m inlet-plane-to-exit span and an overall 5.58 m extent including the forward spinner. These are explicit proportion hypotheses, not manufacturer PW-600 dimensions.

kinematics.author: Kevin Renshaw, Lockheed ASTOVL engineer
kinematics.observations: The B uses a compact axisymmetric nozzle; A/C flaps are longer. A three-bearing swivel duct uses inclined airtight circular bearings and a center segment rotating 180 degrees relative to the forward/aft segments; the first bearing supplies yaw. Total direction travel is 95 degrees. Cooling liner continuity is required across joints.
kinematics.unresolved: The symmetric 23.75-degree joint cuts (95/4), bearing lengths, ring radii, detailed actuator proportions and coupled roll are reconstructed mechanism inputs, not measured PW-600 parts.

integration.observations: Shorter STOVL nozzle, overlapping convergent/divergent flow-path and fairing flaps; A8 throat and A9 exit are distinct.

modelingHypotheses: All component stations, casing sections, panel counts, fan-blade count, accessories, aperture endpoints and material appearance are original visual hypotheses, not component drawings or counted engineering facts.

Sixteen rigid convergent flaps and sixteen divergent flaps hinge at a moving throat, with separate rigid gap seals, fairings and fairing seals. Fixed-size metal pieces move through rotations and translations only. Native normalized command drives an explicitly approximate linear angle cam; this is not a recovered PW-600 mechanism or calibrated A8/A9 schedule.
The upstream annulus and dark centerbody create real rear-view depth. They are core-facing hot hardware; neither identifies the main combustor nor establishes eight injectors.

No third-party image, mesh or texture is included in either runtime engine export. Stand-only external casing/accessories are excluded from the installed export. The inlet face and internal occluder are retained for airframe intake views.

The two oblique circular joints use half-angle geometry and a finite aft straightener. The open throat radius .44 m remains smaller than the neutral joint axial projection radius (.50*cos23.75 degrees = .458 m); neither flow area nor losses are calibrated. The authored engine installation is 0.10 m below the old nozzle axis to fit the source airframe across conversion and yaw.

patent.title: Apparatus for moving rotatable components
patent.supports: Three adjacent duct sections, upstream bearing to engine, two opposed scarfed circular bearing planes, aft section fixed to variable-area outlet, contra-rotation. Patent example planes 65 degrees to duct axis (normal tilt 25 degrees).
patent.limits: Patent topology is not a production F135 drawing. Equal23.75-degree cuts derive from published95-degree full vector with180-degree relative rotation; all detailed dimensions are original hypotheses.

apertureMechanism.supports: Generic axisymmetric convergent/divergent flaps, interposed gap seals, hinge seals, centered sliding seal restraints and external drive links. Hamstra/McCallum section 2.2.1 separately supports internal CD flaps and external fairing flaps.
apertureMechanism.limits: Generic patent does not establish production F135-PW-600 counts, dimensions, pivot coordinates or actuator law. Rigid bisector seals and slotted outer fairings are original reduced kinematics. Nominal plate thickness and 8200 kg/m3 density only supply a declared geometric mass hypothesis; no actual alloy or mass calibration, and no relation to native effective thermal capacities.

qualification: Original approximation; geometry validation is separate from device or photometric qualification.
